plan: This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: I exit when the clock reaches my bid, and if I win, I pay the second-highest bid. Bidding truthfully (equal to my value) is the dominant strategy here, since bidding higher risks winning at a price above my value, and bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. My value is $4, so I will bid exactly $4 to maximize expected profit.

This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my bid only determines when I exit the clock. In second-price auctions, bidding my true value is a dominant strategy - if I bid higher, I risk winning and overpaying above my value; if I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $23.

This is structurally a second-price auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my exit price only matters relative to others' bids. Bidding my true value ($32) is the dominant strategy—if I bid higher, I risk winning at a price above my value; if I bid lower, I risk losing profitable opportunities. Since values are independently drawn and this is a one-shot round, truthful bidding maximizes my expected profit.
